evidence.claim: Article 110 gives the Leader supreme command of the armed forces, war-and-peace authority, and appointment power over key judiciary, media, and military posts; Article 111 provides a temporary replacement council if the office becomes vacant.
evidence.title: Iran (Islamic Republic of) 1979 (rev. 1989) Constitution
evidence.excerpt: Article 110 gives the Leader supreme command of the armed forces, war-and-peace authority, and appointment power over key judiciary, media, and military posts; Article 111 provides a temporary replacement council if the office becomes vacant.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Stable constitutional text reproduced by a reputable legal repository; directly defines authority and constraints relevant to 2022.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct office-level authority held by Ali Khamenei as Supreme Leader.
contrary_evidence: The constitution includes a formal vacancy-replacement mechanism, so the office is powerful but not literally unbounded on paper.

evidence.claim: Khamenei said Iran should not tie its economy to lifting U.S. sanctions and urged officials to govern so sanctions would not hurt the country, while promoting a knowledge-based economy.
evidence.title: Iran's Khamenei says economy should not be tied to U.S. sanctions
evidence.excerpt: Khamenei said Iran should not tie its economy to lifting U.S. sanctions and urged officials to govern so sanctions would not hurt the country, while promoting a knowledge-based economy.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters wire with direct quotations from Khamenei and clear date/setting.
contrary_evidence: This is policy rhetoric, not proof of truthfulness or delivery.
It can be read as strategic framing rather than a factual claim about economic conditions.

evidence.claim: Khamenei said Iran’s future should not depend on the success or collapse of nuclear talks and told officials not to wait for negotiations when planning the country.
evidence.title: Khamenei Says Iran's Future Should Not Be Tied to Nuclear Talks
evidence.excerpt: Khamenei said Iran’s future should not depend on the success or collapse of nuclear talks and told officials not to wait for negotiations when planning the country.
evidence.source_locator: reported remarks from senior officials gathering
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters reporting with a specific attributable statement and date.
contrary_evidence: This does not by itself show deception; it may simply be a negotiating posture.
It does not establish whether his public framing matched internal policy constraints.

evidence.claim: Khamenei accused Western adversaries of being behind women activists challenging Iran’s dress code and said enemy media were attacking Iran to spread doubt.
evidence.title: Iran's Khamenei says Western enemies stoking anti-hijab protests
evidence.excerpt: Khamenei accused Western adversaries of being behind women activists challenging Iran’s dress code and said enemy media were attacking Iran to spread doubt.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters wire with direct quotations and clear identification of the speech context.
contrary_evidence: The statement is political blame-shifting, not a verified factual account.
It is not proof of personal gain or hidden corruption.

evidence.claim: In his first public comments on the protests, Khamenei called them riots, blamed the United States and Israel, and said the death of Mahsa Amini had broken his heart while still denying that the unrest reflected normal public reaction.
evidence.title: Iran's Khamenei blames Israel, US in first comments on protests
evidence.excerpt: In his first public comments on the protests, Khamenei called them riots, blamed the United States and Israel, and said the death of Mahsa Amini had broken his heart while still denying that the unrest reflected normal public reaction.
evidence.source_locator: middle paragraphs containing the quoted speech
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters-reported speech with direct quotation and strong contemporaneous corroboration.
contrary_evidence: He did acknowledge Amini’s death as painful, which is a limited sign of acknowledgment.
The speech still sharply shifted responsibility away from the state and toward foreign enemies.

evidence.claim: Khamenei described the protests as scattered riots designed by the enemy and said the unrest was a clumsy foreign plot against the Iranian nation.
evidence.title: Iran's Khamenei calls anti-government protests 'scattered riots' designed by the enemy
evidence.excerpt: Khamenei described the protests as scattered riots designed by the enemy and said the unrest was a clumsy foreign plot against the Iranian nation.
evidence.source_locator: first paragraphs of the Reuters wire
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters wire reproduced by a major outlet, with direct attribution to Khamenei’s remarks.
contrary_evidence: Still rhetorical rather than documentary proof of deliberate falsehood.
It reinforces the same blame-shifting pattern already seen in October.

evidence.claim: Khamenei warned that Iran’s enemies may try to mobilize workers after failing to topple the Islamic government, framing the protest movement as a hostile external campaign.
evidence.title: Iran leader says 'enemies' may target workers as protests rage
evidence.excerpt: Khamenei warned that Iran’s enemies may try to mobilize workers after failing to topple the Islamic government, framing the protest movement as a hostile external campaign.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters wire summary, though the mirror is less direct than Reuters itself.
contrary_evidence: The claim remains political framing, not a tested factual report.
It does not by itself show concealment or self-enrichment.

evidence.claim: Khamenei praised Basij forces for sacrificing themselves to save people from rioters, explicitly endorsing the militia wing that was central to protest suppression.
evidence.title: Iran's Khamenei praises Basij forces for confronting 'riots'
evidence.excerpt: Khamenei praised Basij forces for sacrificing themselves to save people from rioters, explicitly endorsing the militia wing that was central to protest suppression.
evidence.source_locator: first paragraphs of the Reuters wire
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters wire with direct quotation and clear context.
contrary_evidence: This is supportive of repression, not evidence of personal honesty.
It helps mainly as evidence of tolerance and endorsement of the crackdown narrative.

evidence.claim: OFAC said seven senior leaders in Iran’s government and security apparatus were responsible for shutting down Iran’s internet access and continuing violence against peaceful protesters; the release specifically named the interior minister, communications minister, and an IRGC-linked close associate of the Supreme Leader’s orbit.
evidence.title: Treasury Sanctions Iranian Leaders Responsible for Internet Shutdown and Violent Crackdown on Peaceful Protests
evidence.excerpt: OFAC said seven senior leaders in Iran’s government and security apparatus were responsible for shutting down Iran’s internet access and continuing violence against peaceful protesters; the release specifically named the interior minister, communications minister, and an IRGC-linked close associate of the Supreme Leader’s orbit.
evidence.source_locator: main release text and sanctions rationale sections
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary U.S. government sanctions notice with specific named roles and rationale.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect but material: the named officials acted inside the Khamenei-led system; not a direct personal order from Khamenei in the document.
contrary_evidence: The document does not name Khamenei himself as the actor.
It is a sanctions finding, so it is adversarial but still primary evidence.

evidence.claim: OFAC said additional Iranian officials and entities were involved in the ongoing crackdown on protests and efforts to disrupt digital freedom, including internet throttling, surveillance, and arrests of dissidents.
evidence.title: Treasury Sanctions Iranian Officials and Entities Responsible for Ongoing Crackdown on Protests and Internet Censorship
evidence.excerpt: OFAC said additional Iranian officials and entities were involved in the ongoing crackdown on protests and efforts to disrupt digital freedom, including internet throttling, surveillance, and arrests of dissidents.
evidence.source_locator: opening release text and IRGC Intelligence Organization sections
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary government sanction notice with detailed attribution to specific bodies and conduct.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect but material: the conduct is within the apparatus Khamenei oversees, though the document does not specify his direct personal order.
contrary_evidence: This is still institutional attribution, not a personal confession or asset disclosure.
It proves repression and concealment more clearly than financial self-dealing.

evidence.claim: Treasury said the Iranian government cut off internet access for most citizens to prevent the world from watching its crackdown on peaceful protesters, and the license was issued to help Iranians access outside platforms and services.
evidence.title: U.S. Treasury Issues Iran General License D-2 to Increase Support for Internet Freedom
evidence.excerpt: Treasury said the Iranian government cut off internet access for most citizens to prevent the world from watching its crackdown on peaceful protesters, and the license was issued to help Iranians access outside platforms and services.
evidence.source_locator: opening paragraphs and Deputy Secretary quotation
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary U.S. government statement with explicit causal language about concealment.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect but material: the action is attributed to the Iranian government under Khamenei’s system.
contrary_evidence: The document is a U.S. policy statement, not an internal Iranian record.
It does not isolate Khamenei personally from the broader regime action.

evidence.claim: Iran restricted access to Instagram and WhatsApp as protests grew after Mahsa Amini’s death, according to residents and NetBlocks, limiting key public communication channels.
evidence.title: As unrest grows, Iran restricts access to Instagram, WhatsApp
evidence.excerpt: Iran restricted access to Instagram and WhatsApp as protests grew after Mahsa Amini’s death, according to residents and NetBlocks, limiting key public communication channels.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters wire with contemporaneous technical reporting and named platforms.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect but material: the restriction was imposed by the Iranian state apparatus under Khamenei’s authority.
contrary_evidence: This is an implementation fact, not a statement of intent from Khamenei.
It shows censorship rather than personal enrichment.
